newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Indonesia coffee crop to recover in 96-97 cycle.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee crop to recover in 96-97 cycle.

text.p: After two consecutive years of drought, Indonesia's coffee crop will recover this 1996-1997 cycle (April-March) to bring an output of 8.0 million bags, a top Indonesian coffee consultant said here Wednesday.

Derek Watson, consultant to the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters (AICE), told reporters that the national drive to increase arabica bean output and the general recovery of the harvest will make the crop come in 1.5 million 60-kg bags more than the 6.5 million bags produced in 1994-1995 and 1995-1996.

Watson, who has been in the coffee business for 40 years and was speaking here at the International Coffee Week, known as Sintercafe in Spanish, said production prior to the drought cycle was a steady 7 to 7.5 million bags.
He said despite the higher output Indonesia would not exceed its 6 million bag export limit under the programme designed by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
"We will meet that target but we will not exceed it," Watson said, saying the export quota system was worked out for what the market needs and not based on restricting supply.
Watson said Indonesia's domestic consumption would basically take up all the remaining output. He said in the year 1994-1996 the country averaged national consumption at close to 2 million bags.
He declined to give an estimte of current Indonesia stocks, although highlighted the country did carry working stocks, but not contingent stocks.
